title: Input message catalog (data plane)
description: Messages carried on the WebRTC input DataChannels (`input` and `keys`, see `channels`). Phone -> desktop, with one exception: `hostInfo`, which the desktop sends to the phone once when the `keys` channel opens. DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from ../catalog.json: that one is the signaling control plane and mirrors the sealed SignalingMessage hierarchy in signaling-server, which never sees these. Adding an input type there would claim a parity the server does not have, and would suggest input bytes pass through our servers. They do not (CLAUDE.md architecture invariants).

transport.note: The desktop is the offerer, and an answerer cannot add an m-line the offer lacks, so the host creates the channel before setLocalDescription() and the phone receives it via ondatachannel. No signaling message is involved: the channel is negotiated inside the existing SDP exchange.

channels.why: Pointer samples are absolute and superseded by the next one. A retransmitted coordinate is already wrong, and ordered delivery would stall every sample behind a lost one.

Typing needs every keystroke exactly once and in order. A separate channel, not a mode of `input`: on one reliable channel pointer retransmits would head-of-line block keystrokes, and on one unreliable channel keys would be lost and reordered. Two channels are two SCTP streams, so a lost key stalls only the keys behind it. Created by desktop-host alongside `input`, before the offer, for the same reason.

deferred.note: Ctrl/Cmd/Alt applied to characters typed on the phone's on-screen keyboard. `text` carries characters with no modifier state, and the host types them with no flags; the on-screen modifier bar's latched modifiers wrap only the bar's own keys. Chording a soft-keyboard letter would need the phone to turn the character back into a position (impossible in general: the host's layout is what maps positions to characters) or a `text` field for modifiers that the host applies as flags.

Capturing browser- and OS-reserved combos (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Alt+Tab, Win key) with the Keyboard Lock API in fullscreen, so they reach the desktop instead of the browser. Until then the phone warns (beforeunload, an in-viewer banner) and the on-screen modifier keys are the way to send them. Ctrl <-> Command translation is DONE: the phone does it from `hostInfo`.
